newsitem.title: USA: Lennar announces record third quarter.
newsitem.headline: Lennar announces record third quarter.

text.p: Lennar Corp, a diversified real estate company, announced record earnings for its third quarter, and said on Wednesday that full year earnings should exceed last year's record levels.
Chairman of the board Leonard Miller told Reuters he also expected a good year in 1997.
"All three divisions had an exceptional quarter so there was no single factor, though we are having an exceptional year in housing," he said.
"We think we are going to have an even better year next year because of our entry into California and expansion in Texas," Miller said.
The company reported on Wednesday that revenues for the third quarter ended Aug 31 were $320 million, up 56 percent over the $204.7 million for the third quarter of 1995.
Net earnings for the quarter increased to $23.9 million, or 66 cents per share, up 52 percent over the $15.7 million, or 44 cents per share, reported in the 1995 period.
Revenues for the first nine months of 1996 were $804.8 million, compared with revenues of $596.4 million in the same period of 1995, representing an increase of 35 percent.

Lennar's net earnings for the first nine months of 1996 were $59.4 million, or $1.64 per share, an increase of 18 percent when compared with $50.4 million or $1.40 per share, reported in the first nine months of 1995.

Miller said the strong showing in housing was partly because Lennar operated in four markets, which accounted for between 30 to 40 percent of the total housing sold in the United States -- Florida, California, Arizona and Texas.

Texas was Lennar's strongest expansion market, Miller said, while the company developed a new market in California following the acquisition of the bankrupt Bramalea Corp, which was completed in the third quarter.
New orders in Florida and Arizona were lower.
The average Lennar home cost $146,000, selling usually to first-time buyers, first-time "move-uppers" and retirees.
Earnings for homebuilding operations were up 93 percent, for the financial services division up 30 percent and for the investment division up 23 percent.

"This record third quarter for Lennar, coupled with our strong backlog of homes sold for future delivery, virtually assures that 1996 will be the best year in the company's history," Miller said earlier on Wednesday in a company statement.

The purchase price for Bramalea was about $60 million, which included $50 million paid to acquire Bramalea's debt and about $10 million of advances to Bramalea. The company recorded a substantial deferred tax benefit through the transaction.
